Based on the search results, I can work through this step by step:

1. **Country where Wilfried Gröbner was:** East Germany (German Democratic Republic/GDR) - he was born in Eilenburg, East Germany in 1949 and represented East Germany in the 1976 Olympic Games where they won gold.

2. **Literature of East Germany:** East Germany had its own literary tradition with notable authors like Christa Wolf, Heiner Müller, and others writing during the GDR period.

3. **Country of that literature:** East Germany (the same country)

4. **Border troops of East Germany:** These were the **Grenztruppen der DDR** (GDR Border Troops/Border Guards), a military force responsible for securing East Germany's borders with West Germany and NATO countries during the Cold War era.

5. **Country of those border troops:** **East Germany** (German Democratic Republic/GDR)

The answer is **East Germany** (now part of **Germany** after reunification in 1990). The border troops specifically belonged to the German Democratic Republic (GDR/East Germany) before its dissolution and subsequent reunification with West Germany.

# Wilfried Gröbner
**Wilfried Gröbner** (born 18 December 1949) is a German former footballer and coach who was part of East Germany's gold medal-winning team at the 1976 Olympics.

# Wilfried Gröbner
## Club career
[edit]
The defender played 230 East German top-flight matches for Lokomotive Leipzig.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilfried_Gr%C3%B6bner#cite_note-2)

# Wilfried Gröbner
## International career
[edit]
Between 1976 and 1979 he was part of the East Germany national team.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilfried_Gr%C3%B6bner#cite_note-3) His only appearance for the East Germany Olympic team, during this era still counted as a full international when it was played against another A squad (in this case Poland), was in 1976 the Gold Medal match at the Montreal Olympics. East German won this encounter against Poland 3-1 and became Olympic champion.

# Wilfried Gröbner
## Coaching career
[edit]
Gröbner later was at the coaching helm for Rot-Weiß Erfurt and SSV Reutlingen.

**Wilfried Gröbner** (Eilenburg, 18 dicembre1949) è un allenatore di calcio ed ex calciatoretedesco orientale, dal 1990 tedesco, di ruolo difensore.
Gioca tutta la sua carriera nel Lokomotive Lipsia, per cui segna 18 goal in 230 partite.

Ha collezionato 8 presenze nella Nazionale tedesca orientale. Il debutto avvenne da titolare nell'incontro del 21 aprile 1976 a Cottbus contro l'Algeria (5:0) ma dove giocò solo il primo tempo; l'ultima gara fu a Burgas il 28 febbraio 1979 nella sconfitta contro la Bulgaria (1:0). Ai Giochi Olimpici 1976 giocò soltanto gli ultimi 21 minuti nella finale per la medaglia d'oro contro la Polonia (3:1) entrando al posto di Wolfram Loewe.
Ha allenato il Rot-Weiß Erfurt ed il Reutlingen.

Gioca tutta la sua carriera nel Lokomotive Lipsia, per cui segna 18 goal in 230 partite.
texts.1:
Ha collezionato 8 presenze nella Nazionale tedesca orientale. Il debutto avvenne da titolare nell'incontro del 21 aprile 1976 a Cottbus contro l'Algeria (5:0) ma dove giocò solo il primo tempo; l'ultima gara fu a Burgas il 28 febbraio 1979 nella sconfitta contro la Bulgaria (1:0). Ai Giochi Olimpici 1976 giocò soltanto gli ultimi 21 minuti nella finale per la medaglia d'oro contro la Polonia (3:1) entrando al posto di Wolfram Loewe.
Ha allenato il Rot-Weiß Erfurt ed il Reutlingen.

# Wilfried Gröbner
**Wilfried Gröbner** (born 18 December 1949) is a German former footballer and coach who was part of East Germany's gold medal-winning team at the 1976 Olympics.

# Wilfried Gröbner
## Club career
[edit]
The defender played 230 East German top-flight matches for Lokomotive Leipzig.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilfried_Gr%C3%B6bner#cite_note-2)

# Wilfried Gröbner
## International career
[edit]
Between 1976 and 1979 he was part of the East Germany national team.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilfried_Gr%C3%B6bner#cite_note-3) His only appearance for the East Germany Olympic team, during this era still counted as a full international when it was played against another A squad (in this case Poland), was in 1976 the Gold Medal match at the Montreal Olympics. East German won this encounter against Poland 3-1 and became Olympic champion.

# Wilfried Gröbner
## Coaching career
[edit]
Gröbner later was at the coaching helm for Rot-Weiß Erfurt and SSV Reutlingen.
